question: Which is the most common ore of oxidised mercury that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cinnabar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cinnabar** is the most common ore of oxidised **mercury **that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs.
 
• Cinnabar is a bright red mineral consisting of **mercury sulfide (HgS)**.
 
• It has been used historically as a pigment and is the primary source of mercury.
 
• The mineral forms in a variety of geological environments, often in association with volcanic activity and hot springs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mercury** has various industrial applications, including in thermometers, barometers, and other scientific instruments.
 
• **Exposure to mercury** and its compounds can be highly toxic, affecting the nervous system, digestive system, and immune system.
 
• The extraction and processing of cinnabar to produce mercury must be handled with extreme care to prevent environmental contamination and health hazards.
 
• The use of mercury has declined due to its toxicity and the development of safer alternatives.
